title: AI Agents Wreak Havoc: Five Attacks in Switzerland Breach Power, Water, and Communications Systems, Four Succeed
excerpt: Beyond writing code, booking flights, and conducting research, AI agents have gained another kind of “business”: breaking into critical infrastructure on behalf
content_html:
Beyond writing code, booking flights, and conducting research, AI agents have gained another kind of “business”: breaking into critical infrastructure on behalf of attackers. According to Reuters, the Swiss Federal Office for Cybersecurity (BACS) reported on Thursday (November 26) that five cyberattacks launched by AI agents had occurred in Switzerland in the past few days, targeting companies and critical infrastructure operators.

Five Attacks, Four Successful

The notice shows that four of the five attacks succeeded, and the affected systems were breached. The targets included three critical infrastructure operators. According to Swiss public broadcaster SRF, they were providers of electricity, water, and communications services—systems whose disruption would affect the daily functioning of countless households. The Swiss Federal Office for Cybersecurity did not disclose who was behind the attacks, nor did it explain the specific methods or damage.

AI Agents Lower the Bar for Attacks

Unlike earlier generations of “AI-assisted malware writing,” AI agents can plan autonomously, execute multi-step tasks, and call tools, stringing together reconnaissance, infiltration, and other stages into an automated chain. Attackers only need to give them an objective. This has also become a recent focus for cybersecurity agencies around the world: the more critical the infrastructure, the greater the concern that AI will turn attacks that once required professional teams into operations that are easier to launch. In its notice, BACS advised relevant companies to implement protections, including conducting regular cybersecurity testing.

The notice did not disclose further details, but the signal is clear enough: when AI agents side with attackers, power and water systems that “cannot stop” have become the latest testing ground.
